batchName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did Caesar reportedly say as he crossed the Rubicon?
options: Alea iacta est: “the die is cast”
questions.explanation: Another ancient writer says he quoted a Greek poet instead, and Caesar’s own account never mentions the river.
questions.sourceQuote: he declared "the die is cast" (*alea iacta est*).

questions.question: After which battle did Caesar write veni, vidi, vici?
options: Zela, against a king of Pontus
questions.explanation: “I came, I saw, I conquered” summed up a very short campaign.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar summed up the brief campaign in a letter: "I came, I saw, I conquered" (*veni, vidi, vici*).

questions.question: On which day was Caesar killed?
options: The Ides of March (Idus Martiae), 15 March
questions.explanation: It was the last Senate meeting before he left to fight the Parthians.
questions.sourceQuote: fell on the Ides of March (*Idus Martiae*), 15 March.

questions.question: Why was Caesar’s clementia at Corfinium shrewd?
options: Because Italy did not turn on him
Because it ended the war at once
questions.explanation: Unlike earlier civil-war leaders, he took no revenge and his troops did not plunder.

questions.question: Hailed as rex, Caesar punned: “I am not Rex, but Caesar.” Why was it a pun?
options: Rex means king, and was also a Roman family name
Rex was the name of his horse
Rex was the title of a priest he held
Rex was his nickname in Gaul
questions.explanation: When the tribunes arrested the first man to shout, Caesar had them stripped of office.
questions.sourceQuote: He punned, "I am not Rex, but Caesar," since Rex was also a Roman family name.

questions.question: How many lictores marched before Caesar at his triumphs in 46 BC?
options: Seventy-two, three times a dictator’s usual number
questions.explanation: They carried the fasces, bundles of rods around an axe.
questions.sourceQuote: Seventy-two attendants (*lictores*) marched before him carrying the fasces

questions.question: What did Caesar say he was defending when the civil war began?
questions.explanation: Modern historians doubt ancient claims that he feared prosecution.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar said he was defending his personal honour (*dignitas*).

questions.question: Early in 44 BC Caesar was made dictator perpetuo. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: A flattering Senate also gave him the title “Father of his Country”.
questions.sourceQuote: Early in 44 BC he was made dictator for life (*dictator perpetuo*).
